Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verses 38–41 (part 1 of 2):

Allah ……ʿāqibat al-umūr (41)

On this earth, the forces of evil are at work at all times. The struggle between good and evil, between guidance and misguidance, goes on continually, and this struggle has existed since the time Allah created man and sent him to this earth.

Evil is always arrogant, and falsehood is always armed with power and weapons. The grip of evil is merciless, and its blows are struck without pity. If some of Allah's servants come to know the path of guidance, it blocks their way and turns them away from the truth, whenever a heart is opened to the truth. Therefore it is necessary that faith, truth and goodness have power behind them as well, so that the grip, arrogance, mischief and aggression of falsehood can be checked, and the truth can be protected from enemies and hardships.

It is by no means Allah's will that faith, goodness and truth be left so weak that they cannot confront falsehood on the battlefield. In this matter, the greatest reliance is placed on the faith-power that burns in the hearts of the people of truth, and the zeal for truth in human nature and human conscience is put to use. Because if there is no power of truth to match the forces of falsehood, the people of truth may be affected by it; their steps may falter. The nature of the people of truth can also be corrupted, because patience has a limit too, and the endurance of afflictions has an end, and at a certain point human strength gives way. Allah knows well the hearts and souls of people. That is why Allah has not willed that the believers be put into trial forever. Yes, the use of force may be withheld to the extent that they are preparing for confrontation, the preparations for defence are underway, and the means of jihad are being gathered. When they have completed these tasks, then they are permitted to fight, so that they can repel the aggressive hands of the disbelievers.

Before granting permission to fight, Allah announces that He Himself defends the believers, and that Allah has the power to help and support them.

ʾInna Allāha yudāfiʿu ʿani alladhīna āmanū (22:38): "Surely Allah defends those who have believed." Allah does not love the enemies of the believers, because they have denied the truth and they are also treacherous. Therefore, surely He will humiliate them.

ʾInna Allāha lā yuḥibbu kulla khawwānin kafūr (22:38): "Surely Allah does not love any treacherous, ungrateful one." Allah has decreed that the believers have the full right to defend themselves; their position is correct, also from the standpoint of the rules of war, because they are oppressed, they have not committed aggression, and they are not transgressors.

ʾUdhina lilladhīna yuqātalūna bi-annahum ẓulimū (22:39): "Permission has been given to those against whom war is waged, because they have been wronged." They should be content with this support of Allah. Allah will certainly help them.

Wa-inna Allāha ʿalā naṣrihim la-qadīr (22:39): "And surely Allah is able to give them victory." They have been permitted to take part in this struggle because they are entering this great mission for the whole of humanity; the results of this mission will be beneficial not only for them but for all Muslims, because through it the fundamental rights of freedom of faith and conviction will be established. Moreover, this also provides justification: they have been driven out of their homes and their country without any just cause.

Alladhīna ukhrijū min diyārihim bi-ghayri ḥaqqin illā an yaqūlū rabbunā Allāh (22:40): "They are those who were expelled from their homes unjustly, only for saying, 'Our Lord is Allah.'" And this was a very true statement, one that could ever be uttered; it was most deserving of being repeated again and again. When their expulsion was carried out because of this, it was open arrogance and oppression, and there is no room for any doubt in it. Moreover, the oppressed had no personal enmity with anyone; it was only their ideology that caused them to be expelled. In this conflict, no worldly interest was involved, so that someone could make a pretext of interests, desires or any greed, or use sympathies or any other personal likes and dislikes as a pretext. This was purely an ideological war.

Furthermore, it is also a general principle that every ideology has an absolute need for the power of self-defence.

Wa-law lā daf ʿu Allāhi an-nāsa baʿḍahum bi-baʿḍin lahudimat ṣawāmiʿu wa-biyaʿun wa-ṣalawātun wa-masājidu yudhkaru fīhā ismu Allāhi kathīrā (22:40): "And if Allah did not repel some people by means of others, cloisters, churches, synagogues and mosques, in which the name of Allah is much mentioned, would surely have been demolished." A ṣawmaʿa (cloister) is the place of worship where monks worship. A bīʿa is the place of worship of the Christians; it is larger than a ṣawmaʿa. Ṣalawāt refers to the place of worship of the Jews. Masājid are the places of worship of Muslims.

Although these places are dedicated and sacred for the worship of Allah, all of them can be demolished if there is no power of defence behind them. Those of falsehood have no concern with whether the name of Allah is mentioned in these places; rather, the protection and preservation of these places is possible only when the supporters of a faith stand behind it, possess power of defence, and are able to have the respect for their faith enforced upon the enemy by force. Falsehood is arrogant; it stops only when a power like its own exists on the side of the one it attacks. Merely because truth is truth, falsehood will not refrain from attacking. Therefore, there must be an equal, or rather superior, power behind the truth that can defend it. This is a universal benefit; as long as there are human beings, it will remain so.

Here there is a need to reflect upon those Qur'anic texts whose words are very few but whose meanings are very vast. These texts contain the important secrets of the human self, of life, and of the events of human life.

Allah is granting permission to fight to those against whom the polytheists waged war and inflicted aggression upon them. This is because Allah takes on the responsibility of defending the believers, and He does not like that treacherous disbelievers should commit aggression against the Muslims.

ʾInna Allāha yudāfiʿu ……kafūr (22:38).

"Allah defends those who believe; surely Allah does not love any treacherous, ungrateful disbeliever." Allah has given the Muslims this guarantee: that He will defend them, and whomever Allah defends, it is certain that the enemy cannot harm him in any way. He will prevail over his enemy. Here the question arises: why then does Allah grant them permission to fight? Why has jihad been made obligatory? Why do they fight, in which some are killed, some are wounded, and they must strive, exert themselves, endure difficulties and make sacrifices, and the outcome is that they prevail, although Allah could defend them without their struggle, without any hardship or sacrifice, and without any killing or fighting?

The answer is that Allah's wisdom in this matter is very profound and far-reaching. Allah's love reaches its true station and is very lofty; but according to what we have been able to understand, and according to the capacity of our minds, and according to our experiences, what appears to us is that Allah has not considered it appropriate that the bearers of His call remain lazy and idle, sitting with great indolence, and that Allah's help then comes to them while they sit like princes, merely because they recite the Qur'an, pray, and at all times supplicate before Allah. For these tasks, though all of them are necessary, do not make them capable of supporting and defending the Islamic call. Prayer, worship and supplication are provisions for a soldier, and in battle they serve as moral strength; the believers have an additional weapon which the enemy does not have. The conventional weapons that the enemy has, the Muslims also have; and in addition they have taqwā and constant connection with Allah.

It is Allah's will that the defence of Muslims and believers be carried out by Him through the Muslims and believers themselves, so that they become firm during the course of the struggle. This is because the hidden powers within the human personality awaken only when a person faces danger and is defending himself. In confrontation and war, a person comes out against the enemy with his full strength. In such circumstances every cell of human strength becomes active and ready, so that it may play its part, cooperate with the other cells, and carry out joint actions. As much strength as can be supplied is supplied. In short, he expends the last particle of his strength, and the person reaches that station which is destined for him.

The community that rises carrying the Islamic call has the duty to devote every cell of its strength, its entire reserve of power, the full essence of its capabilities and all its forces to this path, so that its own training and development may be completed, that it may become firm, and that in this way it may be ready to bear the burden of the trust placed upon it.

The victory and success in which the one who triumphs has suffered no hardship, and the success that is obtained very easily and without a thorn pricking, does not bring forth these humble capacities of human workers, because there is no stimulus for their manifestation; the challenge is the real stimulus.

Moreover, the success that comes very comfortably and as if sitting idle is easily converted into failure and is lost in the same way. Since it comes for free and the one who succeeds has paid no price for it, he holds no value for it in his eyes. Furthermore, the capacities of those to whom it comes while sitting idle are not tested in experience, because when their hidden powers are not awakened to obtain it, how will they awaken to defend it? Therefore defence becomes impossible for them.

This practical and intuitive training is acquired by a person only when he has experienced both victory and defeat, has seen its pomp, has seen strength and weakness, has known both advance and retreat, and has tasted the joy and the bitterness of both. Hope and fear, joy and grief, contentment and anguish, the sense of weakness and the awareness of strength: all of this he has seen on the battlefield.

Moreover, he has witnessed both the unity of ideologies and ideological disunity. He experiences harmonizing different tendencies. He is aware of the centres of strength and the points of weakness within the community, and he knows how to manage affairs in every kind of situation. All these stages are necessary for the community and group that is to carry the Islamic call forward, and this cannot be achieved unless someone actually enters the battle.

For this reason, and because of other hidden wisdoms known only to Allah, Allah has decreed that He defends the Muslims through the Muslims themselves, and He did not declare that this would be a morsel ready-made and served to them from the heavens.

Sometimes the descent of help is delayed for oppressed people who are expelled from their homes and are persecuted solely because they affirm their Lord as one. They affirm only Allah as Lord, yet there is a profound wisdom of Allah hidden in this.

Sometimes help is delayed because the bearers of the Islamic call are not yet mature, and they have weaknesses. Their strengths are not united. The Islamic elements have not brought all the reserves of their strength onto the field. If help came in such a state of immaturity, they would quickly lose it.

Sometimes help is also delayed because it is the will of Allah that believers pour their entire strength into this path, squeeze out their last capital and strength, keep nothing in reserve, and stake everything. As long as they have not done this, help does not come.

Sometimes help also does not come because Allah gives the believers the opportunity to try all their methods, so that they come to know that this help does not come merely because of their own strengths; rather, Allah's help comes when the believers have exhausted their last reserves of strength, wealth and capacities, and nothing remains before them but the help of Allah. Then help arrives.

Sometimes Allah's help is also postponed so that the community of believers reaches the standard of connection with Allah that is desired; they meet with difficulties and endure them, they face painful outcomes and are patient, and they are given the opportunity to expend all their strength, until the situation becomes such that no support remains except Allah, and no point remains for the focus of attention except Allah. This connection with Allah then also guarantees that after help has come and victory has been granted, the community remains on the straight path. It does not then abandon its way; it does not let go of the path of truth, justice and goodness, because of which victory was granted to it.

Sometimes God's help does not come because the community's struggle, its spending and its sacrifices are not done purely for the pleasure of God. Its fighting is for worldly interests, or it fights out of personal grudge, or there is show in its striving, whereas God's intention is that the struggle in the way of God be solely for God, and only in the way of God. No other thought should be attached to it; in the conscious and subconscious minds of the workers there should be no aim other than the pleasure of God.

The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked whether a person fights out of zeal (hamiyyah), or out of bravery, or to display his personality, which of these wars is fi sabilillah (in the way of God). The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Whoever fights so that the word of God becomes supreme, that alone is fi sabilillah." (Man qatala litakuna kalimatullahi hiya al-ulya fa-huwa fi sabilillah.)

Sometimes Islamic forces are not successful because the evil against which the community is working contains some aspect of good. God grants respite to that evil so that He may leave it utterly bare of any good, so that if destruction comes, it comes upon pure evil with no aspect of good in it, and so that not even a particle of good is lost along with evil.

Sometimes God's help does not come because the falsehood against which the Muslim community and the believing group are at war has not become clearly exposed and fully manifest in the eyes of the common people. In such circumstances, if evil is defeated, there will still be found among society some people who support and assist evil, who have not yet understood its deceit, and who have not grasped its corruption and decline and are not convinced of it. Therefore some roots of this evil are present even in the minds of righteous people who are unaware of the reality. For this reason God keeps falsehood in power for a period, so that the minds of all people become clear, and when it is annihilated, there should not remain in society even one eye that weeps over it.

Sometimes the delay in help is also because society is not yet ready to accept the truth, and is not fit to bear up the truth, whose bearer and caller is the believing group. If in such circumstances the truth is given help, even then it will not find stability, and a reaction will begin from within society itself. Therefore it is God's will that the struggle between truth and falsehood continue for some further period, so that society becomes ready to welcome the truth.

These may be the reasons, and there may be other reasons which only God knows. Occasionally, the help of God is delayed. The workers must give greater sacrifices, their trials increase, but in the end victory and triumph belong to the believing group, and during the period of struggle God's guarantee of protection remains firmly in place.

The reality is that attaining God's help has certain conditions. There are requirements that must be fulfilled. It has a price that must be paid. It has certain causes that must be provided, and for it a specific atmosphere must be created (remember that this is not mere manna and salwa).

"Indeed, God will surely help those who help Him; indeed God is All-Strong, All-Mighty. Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong; and with God rests the outcome of all affairs." (Surah al-Hajj 22:40–41)

This is God's emphatic promise, a most trustworthy promise, an unbreakable rule, that whoever helps Him, God will surely help. But the question mark remains: which people does God help, so that they may be considered worthy of help? For God is Strong and Mighty, and His allies are never defeated. So who are they? They are these:

"Those whom, if We establish them in the land..." (22:41): if help comes and they are given sovereign authority, then "they will establish prayer" (22:41): they will worship God and turn to Him in utmost obedience, humility, and submission.

"And give zakah" (22:41): they will pay the right of wealth. They will overcome the natural stinginess of the self, purify it from greed and avarice, overcome the whisperings of Satan, and remove the cracks found within the community and society. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verses 42–44:

Lesson No. 146 at a Glance

The previous lesson concluded with the point that war is permitted in defence of ideas, beliefs and the symbols of the community. Those who fulfil the demands of the Islamic way of life will also receive complete divine support from Allah, on the condition that they have themselves established the Islamic system of life within their own community.

Furthermore, the deniers and the polytheists are also directed to this: if their hearts and minds are functioning, they should reflect, because the one who is blind of eyes is not truly blind; rather, the real blind one is the one whose beating heart in his chest is blind.

Moreover, by nullifying the cunning of Satan, He causes His verses to become firmly implanted in the minds of people of sound disposition. As for those whose hearts are diseased, or whose hearts are disbelieving, they will remain entangled in doubt until they witness their evil end.

This entire lesson consists of signs and wonders of the hand of divine power. Allah's hand has been set in motion to advance the call of Islam, but the results will become visible only when those bearing the call fulfil their obligations in the best manner and fulfil the demands that were explained earlier, namely in the previous lesson.

Lesson No. 146: Explanation of the Verses

42 ... to 57

﴿And if they deny you, then indeed the people of Noah, and 'Ad and Thamud, denied before them, and the people of Abraham and the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan; and Musa was denied. So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them; and how was My rejection?﴾ (22:42–44)

Secondly, because the miracles that Musa brought were very clear, and moreover, Musa encountered very great events. In the cases of all these prophets, Allah gave the disbelievers respite for a time, just as respite is now being given to the Quraysh, and after that He seized them with great severity. The interrogative style here is for further warning and for expressing astonishment.

﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ (22:44) Naker (nakir) means a rejection so severe that it carries a suggestion of change. The answer to this question is known: it was a terrible punishment. The flood, the sinking into the earth, destruction, annihilation, earthquakes, ruin, and seizing them with terror through storm and thunderclap, and destroying them.

Allah's hand has been set in motion to advance the call of Islam, but the results will become visible only when those bearing the call fulfil their obligations in the best manner and fulfil the demands that were explained earlier, namely in the previous lesson.

Lesson No. 146: Explanation of the Verses

42 ... to 57

Secondly, because the miracles that Musa brought were very clear, and moreover, Musa encountered very great events. In the cases of all these prophets, Allah gave the disbelievers respite for a time, just as respite is now being given to the Quraysh, and after that He seized them with great severity. The flood, the sinking into the earth, destruction, annihilation, earthquakes, ruin, and seizing them with terror through storm and thunderclap, and destroying them.

Previous destroyed nations, a comprehensive commentary after a very brief glance.

{Fa-ka'ayyin min …… mashid} (45)

Destroyed settlements of this kind are countless. The style of the speech presents the scenes of the destruction of these peoples as a single picture, so that a person says: these are the ruins of destroyed settlements. Great palaces lie fallen upon their roofs, although they had stood upon their walls. When a wall falls, the roofs come down, and the whole structure of the building lies upon them. In this way the scene becomes extremely frightening, heart-rending and impactful. This scene deserves that its former and present condition be considered. When a person walks among ruins, they appear very desolate, and if anyone wishes to take a lesson from them, he can take it, and the fear of God may arise in a person.

The traces of these large villages are before us: their buildings have fallen upon their roofs, their wells lie empty, and no one is seen coming to them or going from them. At some time they were crowded with people. Great structures stand, but there is no human being, not even any living thing. On the screen of imagination, images arise that at some time there was bustle here!

After showing these scenes, the Qur'an, with stern warning, asks: have the polytheists never reflected upon these ruins?

Aw adhanun yasma'una biha (22:36) "Or ears with which they hear." So that they would ask these ruins where the inhabitants of these places went, why these wells lie empty, and why these palaces were laid waste.

Do these people not have intellect? They see, but nothing they see reaches their understanding. They hear, but they take no lesson.

"The truth is that it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts that are in the breasts are blind." But the conduct of these people is entirely the opposite. Instead of taking a lesson, believing, and fearing the punishment of God, these people demand that this punishment come upon them quickly, although God has postponed it for some wisdom.

This is always the way of the wrongdoers in every age. They see with their own eyes the ruins of the wrongdoers of the past. The people may be showing haste, but Allah will bring it at its own time. The people's reckoning of time is one thing, and Allah's reckoning is another.

﴿But indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (22:47). Those ruins and the peoples destroyed in them were also granted respite by Allah, but that respite did not benefit them, because according to Allah's sunnah their destruction had already been decreed.

It is surprising that the polytheists of Makkah demand punishment and mock Allah's warning simply because Allah has granted them respite.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 22, verses 52–54 (part 1 of 2):

Wa ma arsalna ... sirat mustaqim (45)

Many reports have come down concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, and countless exegetes have transmitted them. Ibn Kathir has said that all these reports are mursal (broken in their chain), and that the chain of none of them is sahih (sound). And Allah knows best.

Among these reports, the most detailed is that of Ibn Abi Hatim, who transmitted it through Musa, Abu Musa, Kufi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Shu'bi, Muhammad ibn Filj, Musa, Uqba, Ibn Shihab. Ibn Shihab says: At the time when Surah al-Najm was revealed, the polytheists used to say: If this man mentions our gods in good terms, we would acknowledge his words and accept his companions too. But he does not criticise the Jews and Christians the way he abuses our gods and mentions them with evil. At that time it was hard for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that the polytheists of Makkah denied him and gave torment to his followers. He was very grieved at the misguidance of these people. There was a great desire in his heart that these people should accept guidance. When Surah al-Najm was revealed, he recited it:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ (53:19–20) ... ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female?﴾ (53:21) [Qur'an 53:19–21]

At that very moment, Satan, in connection with the mention of these idols, uttered some words of his own. He said:

"Indeed, they are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is surely that which is hoped for."

These words were added by Satan on his own, as a trial. These words settled in the heart of every polytheist of Makkah. They began to repeat them and gave one another good news, saying that Muhammad had abandoned his religion and returned to his former religion and the religion of his people. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while reciting Surah al-Najm, reached its end, he prostrated, and the Muslims who were listening also prostrated, and the polytheists who were listening also prostrated. Walid ibn Mughirah was a great man; he took some dust in his hand and prostrated upon it. Both groups were astonished that they had prostrated along with the prostration of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Muslims' astonishment was that the polytheists had prostrated with them without having believed or been certain, because the words Satan had uttered had not been heard by the Muslims; only the polytheists had heard them. So the polytheists were content, because Satan had inserted his phrases into the recitation (qira'at) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and had given the polytheists the assurance that these words had been recited by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the surah; so they prostrated out of reverence for their gods. This matter spread among the people. Satan spread this report greatly, to the extent that the news reached Abyssinia, and the Muslims there heard it. The Muslims there were under the leadership of Uthman ibn Maz'un. It reached them that the people of Makkah had become Muslims, that they had prayed together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they also learnt that Walid ibn Mughirah had taken up dust in his palm and prostrated upon it. It was also learnt that now the Muslims were in peace and security in Makkah. So these emigrants returned very quickly from there. Allah abrogated the words of Satan, made His verses firm, and protected the Qur'an from this fabrication. On this occasion this verse was revealed:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke [or wished], Satan threw [some vanity] into his wish. But Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah makes His verses precise. And Allah is Knowing and Wise. That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and who are hardened in heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension. And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, and their hearts will humbly submit to Him. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path.﴾ (22:52–54)

When Allah declared His decision and disavowed the nonsense that Satan had tossed, the polytheists turned back on their heels, adopted misguidance, and began hostility toward the Muslims, and indeed intensified their harshness.

Ibn Kathir says that Baghawi, in his tafsir, collected the full narrations from Ibn Abbas, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi also collected them in this way. Then he raised the question of how this event could occur when Allah has guaranteed the infallibility of Muhammad (ﷺ) in this matter. After this he cited the answers of various people. The most profound answer is that Satan had put these phrases into the ears of the polytheists. The polytheists thought that perhaps these phrases too had been recited by Muhammad (ﷺ), whereas the reality was that these were uttered by Satan and not by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Imam Bukhari says that Ibn Abbas said [this].

The meaning of "fi umniyatihi" is that Satan inserted these phrases into his words. Allah nullified them and made His verses firm.

Mujahid says: the meaning of "idha tamanna" is "idha qala" (when he spoke). Therefore it is said "umniyat qiratahu", i.e., his recitation.

Baghawi says that most exegetes have said that tamanna here means "talla", i.e., he recited and read the Book of Allah.

"Alqa al-Shaytan fi umniyatihi" means: "Satan cast into their mixture." Ibn Jarir says that tamanna means "talla" (he recited), and that this sense appears more appropriate for explaining the meaning of the discourse.

This is the summary of the reports and of those traditions which are called the "gharaniq" hadith. This hadith has no foundation in terms of its chain. The scholars of hadith say: the compilers of the authentic collections did not take up this hadith, nor is there any sound and connected chain for it through reliable narrators. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar says: We are not aware of this hadith being related from the Prophet (ﷺ) through any noteworthy connected chain anywhere. And in terms of its subject, it clashes with the fundamental principle of Islam, namely the doctrine of the infallibility of the Prophet (ﷺ) in regard to the matter that Satan could have a role in the work of conveying the Message.

Orientalists and critics of Islam have shown great interest in this hadith. They have widely publicised it and gathered further hostile statements around it, though they have said nothing worthy of being accepted as proof. Rather, even discussing this subject seems pointless.

Within these verses themselves there are testimonies from which it becomes clear that such a thing is not even possible, or that such an individual incident befell the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The gist of the verses is that what is mentioned in them has been the experience of all messengers: "And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he wished, Satan threw into his wish. Thus Allah abolishes what Satan throws in, and makes His verses firm." Therefore, what is mentioned in this verse is a common attribute among all prophets and messengers, and it relates to their human nature, and this is not contrary to the infallibility assigned to messengers.

This is precisely the point that we shall endeavour to explain here, God willing. The true intent is known to Allah alone; what we set out as exegesis reflects our human faculties only to a certain degree. When messengers are assigned the duty of conveying Allah's message to people, the most beloved thing to them is that people should gather at their call, comprehend the good they have brought from Allah, and submit to them. But many difficulties arise in the face of their call. Messengers are human beings, human life is limited, and they know this reality well. Their wish is to draw people quickly toward their call. For instance, it may occur to their hearts that if they were to reach a compromise with the people, and remain silent for the time being on matters that are difficult for them to give up, such as their customs, traditions, and inherited rites, then perhaps people would come to the call; and once they accept the call, it would be possible for them to abandon those inherited habits, which are now very dear to them. For instance, they might show leniency in minor matters and bring them into the call through some means, in the hope that once inside, they would be trained and their un-Islamic habits would fall away.

In short, messengers and prophets have made many such wishes, relating to the spread and propagation of their call, whereas Allah's will was that the bearers of the call should carry it forward firmly upon its complete principles, in accordance with the subtle values of Islamic da'wah and with the measure "Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve" (18:29). For in Allah's decree, the proper conduct of Islamic da'wah is that it be purely principled, and that no human scheme or desire be mixed into it, so that da'wah proceeds on genuine principles and according to those standards, even though by this method there may be a loss in numbers at the beginning. For if da'wah remains according to standards based on its principles, eventually such persons too will accept the call, and they will accept it with even greater influence and goodness than those persons, and the da'wah will remain pure and sound, straight upon its path, with no crookedness arising in it, and no deviation whatsoever.

In the wishes of man, and in the words which the messenger uses to express those wishes, Satan finds an opportunity to scheme and divert the da'wah from its true path. Thus Satan creates doubts in the ijtihadi matters of spreading the da'wah, but Allah repels the mischief of Satan, and in such matters a firm command comes from Allah, and the messengers are told to convey that firm decision to the people. And the lapses that arose in the hearts of messengers and prophets in ijtihadi matters relating to the spread of the da'wah are clarified by Allah, just as some of the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was clarified.

This is Satan's scheme, and Allah nullifies it, and a firm command comes, and doubt does not remain; a firm verse takes the place of ijtihadi error. Allah is Knowing and Wise. As for those in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy and deviation, or whose hearts have become stone, that is, disbelievers and obstinate opponents, they find an opportunity for argument and questioning in such matters.

"Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension" (22:53). [Rather], those who have been given knowledge and recognition, their hearts become content with this clarification and decisive command, and they grasp the wisdom of Allah's command.

"Indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path" (22:54). In the life of the Prophet (ﷺ) and in the history of Islamic da'wah we find such examples. In their light we do not need that interpretation which Ibn Jarir has indicated.

The story of Ibn Umm Maktum appears here. He was a blind and poor man. He came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me that knowledge which Allah has taught you." He kept repeating this. At that time the Messenger of Allah was speaking with Walid ibn Mughirah, who was among the distinguished leaders of Quraysh, and the Prophet desired that he become a Muslim. Ibn Umm Maktum did not know that the Messenger of Allah was engaged in such an important matter. The Messenger of Allah disliked his repeated interruption on this occasion and turned away from him. Then Allah revealed a surah in this regard, in which a somewhat harsh word was addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you perceive? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him. As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. And not upon you is any blame if he does not purify himself. But as for him who came to you striving, while he fears [Allah], from him you are distracted. No! Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it.﴾ (80:1–11)

Thus Allah returned the da'wah of Islam to its correct and extremely subtle values and standards, and thus corrected the conduct of the Messenger of Allah, who had given preference to the words of the leaders of Quraysh, merely in the hope that they would accept Islam and that a large number of common people would accept Islam along with them. Allah established, as the correct principle and method of da'wah, that more important than the acceptance of Islam by the great men of Quraysh is that the da'wah of Islam proceed on its correct lines. Thus He nullified the whisper which Satan had cast into the desire of the Messenger of Allah, namely that if the great men of Quraysh accepted Islam, the da'wah would spread quickly. Allah, by sending down His decisive verses, corrected this attitude, and the hearts of the believers became content.

After this, the Prophet (ﷺ) greatly honoured Ibn Umm Maktum. Whenever he saw him, he would say: "Welcome to the one because of whom my Lord rebuked me." He would ask him: "Do you need anything?" On one occasion he appointed him as his deputy (khalifah) in Madinah during his absence.

Imam Muslim has related in his Sahih, through Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, Israil, Hamdam ibn Shuruʿ, then from his father, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who says: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), six men in number. The polytheists said: Send these people away, they go ahead of us." He says: I was among them, Ibn Mas'ud was there, a man of Hudhayl was there, Bilal was there, and two other men whose names I have forgotten. Something came into the heart of the Messenger of Allah. Allah knows what came into it. He said something in his heart, so Allah revealed this verse."

And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. ﴿Ya'udhuna rabbahum bil-ghadati wal-'ashiyyi yuridunna wajhah﴾. Here too, Allah set out the extremely precise standards of the Islamic call, and before the whisper of Satan on this point was expressed, Allah depicted it. Perhaps the Prophet ﷺ thought that in future these poor people should not sit in gatherings with the leaders of Quraysh. Yet in the sight of Allah, the value of the Islamic call was superior to those leaders of Quraysh. Moreover, the importance of the values and standards of the call was greater than the Islam of a thousand people who would have supported the movement under the allegiance of those leaders of Quraysh, and whose support the Messenger of Allah ﷺ desired. Allah knew well the true centres of strength for the movement. The real strength of the movement lay in its walking its own path with steadfastness, and not caring for any person or any custom.

The same happened in the incident of Zaynab bint Jahsh. She was the paternal cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given her in marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah. Zayd was a freed slave of the Prophet ﷺ and was known as Zayd ibn Muhammad. The marriage of Zaynab did not succeed in married life. The custom of the Jahiliyyah was that if an adopted son (mutabanni) died or divorced his wife, his adoptive father would not marry her. This was considered shameful. It was Allah's will that this custom be abolished, just as the practice of attributing a son to someone other than his father had been prohibited. Allah had commanded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that if Zayd divorced his wife, he should marry her, so that this custom would be nullified. But the Prophet ﷺ kept this matter hidden in his heart and told no one. Whenever Zayd complained about his wife, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would advise him, "Keep your wife." The meaning of the Prophet ﷺ was that if Zayd divorced her, he would have to marry her, and according to the custom of the Arabs, he disliked this. The Prophet ﷺ kept this matter concealed until Zayd, having become fed up, divorced Zaynab. Allah revealed the Qur'an concerning this and made clear what was in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, and the purpose of Islamic law regarding adopted sons was fulfilled. So Allah said:

﴿Wa-idh taqulu lil-ladhi an'ama Allahu 'alayhi wa-an'amta 'alayhi amsik 'alayka zawjaka wa-ittaqi Allah. Wa-tukhfi fi nafsika ma Allahu mubdihi wa-takhshan-nas wa-Allahu ahaqqu an takhshahu. Falamma qada Zaydun minha watarfa zawwajnakaha likay la yakuna 'alal-mu'minina haraj fi azwaji adi'ya'ihim idha qadau minhunna watara. Wa-kana amru Allahi maf'ula﴾ (33:37 according to the Urdu rendering: "O Prophet, remember when you were saying to the one on whom Allah and you had bestowed favour, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' while you were concealing within yourself what Allah would make manifest, and you were fearing the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. Then when Zayd had fulfilled his need from her, We married her to you, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they had fulfilled their need from them. And the command of Allah is always carried out.")

Aisha said that if Muhammad ﷺ had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿Wa-tukhfi fi nafsika ma Allahu mubdihi wa-takhshan-nas wa-Allahu ahaqqu an takhshahu﴾, "While you were concealing within yourself what Allah would make manifest, and you were fearing the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him."

Thus Allah abolishes what Satan throws in, and makes His verses firm." Therefore, what is mentioned in this verse is a common attribute among all prophets and messengers, and it relates to their human nature, and this is not contrary to the infallibility assigned to messengers.

This is precisely the point that we shall endeavour to explain here, God willing. The true intent is known to Allah alone; what we set out as exegesis reflects our human faculties only to a certain degree. When messengers are assigned the duty of conveying Allah's message to people, the most beloved thing to them is that people should gather at their call, comprehend the good they have brought from Allah, and submit to them. But many difficulties arise in the face of their call. Messengers are human beings, human life is limited, and they know this reality well. Their wish is to draw people quickly toward their call. For instance, it may occur to their hearts that if they were to reach a compromise with the people, and remain silent for the time being on matters that are difficult for them to give up, such as their customs, traditions, and inherited rites, then perhaps people would come to the call; and once they accept the call, it would be possible for them to abandon those inherited habits, which are now very dear to them. For instance, they might show leniency in minor matters and bring them into the call through some means, in the hope that once inside, they would be trained and their un-Islamic habits would fall away.

In short, messengers and prophets have made many such wishes, relating to the spread and propagation of their call, whereas Allah's will was that the bearers of the call should carry it forward firmly upon its complete principles, in accordance with the subtle values of Islamic da'wah and with the measure "Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve" (18:29). For in Allah's decree, the proper conduct of Islamic da'wah is that it be purely principled, and that no human scheme or desire be mixed into it, so that da'wah proceeds on genuine principles and according to those standards, even though by this method there may be a loss in numbers at the beginning. For if da'wah remains according to standards based on its principles, eventually such persons too will accept the call, and they will accept it with even greater influence and goodness than those persons, and the da'wah will remain pure and sound, straight upon its path, with no crookedness arising in it, and no deviation whatsoever.

In the wishes of man, and in the words which the messenger uses to express those wishes, Satan finds an opportunity to scheme and divert the da'wah from its true path. Thus Satan creates doubts in the ijtihadi matters of spreading the da'wah, but Allah repels the mischief of Satan, and in such matters a firm command comes from Allah, and the messengers are told to convey that firm decision to the people. And the lapses that arose in the hearts of messengers and prophets in ijtihadi matters relating to the spread of the da'wah are clarified by Allah, just as some of the conduct of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was clarified.

This is Satan's scheme, and Allah nullifies it, and a firm command comes, and doubt does not remain; a firm verse takes the place of ijtihadi error. Allah is Knowing and Wise. As for those in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy and deviation, or whose hearts have become stone, that is, disbelievers and obstinate opponents, they find an opportunity for argument and questioning in such matters.

"Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension" (22:53). [Rather], those who have been given knowledge and recognition, their hearts become content with this clarification and decisive command, and they grasp the wisdom of Allah's command.

"Indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path" (22:54). In the life of the Prophet (ﷺ) and in the history of Islamic da'wah we find such examples. In their light we do not need that interpretation which Ibn Jarir has indicated.

The story of Ibn Umm Maktum appears here. He was a blind and poor man. He came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me that knowledge which Allah has taught you." He kept repeating this. At that time the Messenger of Allah was speaking with Walid ibn Mughirah, who was among the distinguished leaders of Quraysh, and the Prophet desired that he become a Muslim. Ibn Umm Maktum did not know that the Messenger of Allah was engaged in such an important matter. The Messenger of Allah disliked his repeated interruption on this occasion and turned away from him. Then Allah revealed a surah in this regard, in which a somewhat harsh word was addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you perceive? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him. As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. And not upon you is any blame if he does not purify himself. But as for him who came to you striving, while he fears [Allah], from him you are distracted. No! Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it.﴾ (80:1–11)

Thus Allah returned the da'wah of Islam to its correct and extremely subtle values and standards, and thus corrected the conduct of the Messenger of Allah, who had given preference to the words of the leaders of Quraysh, merely in the hope that they would accept Islam and that a large number of common people would accept Islam along with them. Allah established, as the correct principle and method of da'wah, that more important than the acceptance of Islam by the great men of Quraysh is that the da'wah of Islam proceed on its correct lines. Thus He nullified the whisper which Satan had cast into the desire of the Messenger of Allah, namely that if the great men of Quraysh accepted Islam, the da'wah would spread quickly. Allah, by sending down His decisive verses, corrected this attitude, and the hearts of the believers became content.

After this, the Prophet (ﷺ) greatly honoured Ibn Umm Maktum. Whenever he saw him, he would say: "Welcome to the one because of whom my Lord rebuked me." He would ask him: "Do you need anything?" On one occasion he appointed him as his deputy (khalifah) in Madinah during his absence.

Imam Muslim has related in his Sahih, through Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Asadi, Israil, Hamdam ibn Shuruʿ, then from his father, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who says: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), six men in number. The polytheists said: Send these people away, they go ahead of us." He says: I was among them, Ibn Mas'ud was there, a man of Hudhayl was there, Bilal was there, and two other men whose names I have forgotten. Something came into the heart of the Messenger of Allah. Allah knows what came into it. He said something in his heart, so Allah revealed this verse."

And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. ﴿Ya'udhuna rabbahum bil-ghadati wal-'ashiyyi yuridunna wajhah﴾. Here too, Allah set out the extremely precise standards of the Islamic call, and before the whisper of Satan on this point was expressed, Allah depicted it. Perhaps the Prophet ﷺ thought that in future these poor people should not sit in gatherings with the leaders of Quraysh. Yet in the sight of Allah, the value of the Islamic call was superior to those leaders of Quraysh. Moreover, the importance of the values and standards of the call was greater than the Islam of a thousand people who would have supported the movement under the allegiance of those leaders of Quraysh, and whose support the Messenger of Allah ﷺ desired. Allah knew well the true centres of strength for the movement. The real strength of the movement lay in its walking its own path with steadfastness, and not caring for any person or any custom.

The same happened in the incident of Zaynab bint Jahsh. She was the paternal cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had given her in marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah. Zayd was a freed slave of the Prophet ﷺ and was known as Zayd ibn Muhammad. The marriage of Zaynab did not succeed in married life. The custom of the Jahiliyyah was that if an adopted son (mutabanni) died or divorced his wife, his adoptive father would not marry her. This was considered shameful. It was Allah's will that this custom be abolished, just as the practice of attributing a son to someone other than his father had been prohibited. Allah had commanded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that if Zayd divorced his wife, he should marry her, so that this custom would be nullified. But the Prophet ﷺ kept this matter hidden in his heart and told no one. Whenever Zayd complained about his wife, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would advise him, "Keep your wife." The meaning of the Prophet ﷺ was that if Zayd divorced her, he would have to marry her, and according to the custom of the Arabs, he disliked this. The Prophet ﷺ kept this matter concealed until Zayd, having become fed up, divorced Zaynab. Allah revealed the Qur'an concerning this and made clear what was in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, and the purpose of Islamic law regarding adopted sons was fulfilled. So Allah said:

﴿Wa-idh taqulu lil-ladhi an'ama Allahu 'alayhi wa-an'amta 'alayhi amsik 'alayka zawjaka wa-ittaqi Allah. Wa-tukhfi fi nafsika ma Allahu mubdihi wa-takhshan-nas wa-Allahu ahaqqu an takhshahu. Falamma qada Zaydun minha watarfa zawwajnakaha likay la yakuna 'alal-mu'minina haraj fi azwaji adi'ya'ihim idha qadau minhunna watara. Wa-kana amru Allahi maf'ula﴾ (33:37 according to the Urdu rendering: "O Prophet, remember when you were saying to the one on whom Allah and you had bestowed favour, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' while you were concealing within yourself what Allah would make manifest, and you were fearing the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. Then when Zayd had fulfilled his need from her, We married her to you, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they had fulfilled their need from them. And the command of Allah is always carried out.")

Aisha said that if Muhammad ﷺ had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿Wa-tukhfi fi nafsika ma Allahu mubdihi wa-takhshan-nas wa-Allahu ahaqqu an takhshahu﴾, "While you were concealing within yourself what Allah would make manifest, and you were fearing the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him."

In this way Allah established His law and its rulings, and also made clear that which was causing unease in the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, namely that people regard marriage to the wife of an adopted son as wrong. Here too Allah closed the path of Satan. Those in whose hearts there is a disease, or whose hearts are hard towards the Islamic call, continued to use this incident as a means of sedition, and to this day the enemies of Islam use it as a means of sedition.

This is the matter on which our hearts have been satisfied in the interpretation of this verse. Allah alone is the guide to the right path. After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the leadership of the Islamic call also sometimes tries to draw highly influential people towards the Islamic call, and in the beginning overlooks some matters required by the call. They do this with the motive that the Islamic call may flourish and quickly attain dominance. The view of such leadership is that these matters are not the fundamental matters of the call. They are lenient with these influential people in these matters so that they do not become alienated from the call and do not adopt hostility toward it.

These people also adopt certain means and methods that are incompatible with the precise standards and values of the Islamic call, and these matters do not fit with the simple and straightforward way of the Islamic call. They do this so that the call may spread quickly and succeed. They adopt these matters for the sake of the interest of the call, performing them as a form of ijtihad (independent reasoning), whereas the interest of the Islamic call lies in not deviating from its true method even by a particle's weight, neither in less nor in more, in any matter. As for the results, they are matters of the unseen; only Allah knows about them. Therefore, no bearer of the call should take the reckoning of results into his own hands. The duty of the bearers of the call is only this: that they proceed straight forward with the Islamic call. Success lies only in walking the true path of the Islamic call.

The Qur'an clearly states that it enters upon the bearers of the Islamic call through their desires and wishes, so that in this way it may enter into the ranks of the Islamic call. As for the prophets, Allah had guaranteed their infallibility. It was not possible for Satan to interfere through the natural desires of the prophets. But the leadership that comes later does not know this. It should be extremely vigilant and act with great caution, lest they be doing something they believe to be for the spread and success of the best call of Islam, considering it to be in the interest of the call, while in reality it is Satanic interference. Callers should remove the very phrase "the interest of the call" from their dictionaries, because it is a place of slipping, and it is from this place that Satan attacks. When Satan cannot enter through the personal interests of individuals, then he attacks through the interest of the call. The "interest of the call" has now become an idol. Today the proponents of truth worship it greatly, but under this garb they shy away from the true method of the call. Therefore, the leadership of the Islamic call should not forget the true method of the call, should reflect carefully upon this method, and in particular should not pay attention to the view that such and such a thing should not be done because it poses a danger to the call or to the workers. I say that the real danger is precisely this: that the bearers of the call abandon the true method of the call, for whatever reason, and deviate from the right path, whether this deviation be small or great. Allah knows the interest of His call better than we do, and we are responsible and accountable only for preserving and making the call succeed. Our duty is only one: that we do not deviate from our method and do not swerve in the slightest from our straight path.

At the end comes a warning: you should strive to protect the Islamic call from satanic whisperings. It is not your responsibility that people believe or that the call succeeds. If the disbelievers do not accept it, they are in fact in doubt about it, and for them, in waiting, is a painful and humiliating punishment.

Lesson No. 741: A Glance

The previous lesson ended on the theme that, in the Hereafter, the fate of believers and deniers will be decided, when sovereignty will belong to Allah alone. The argument was that Allah always protects His Messengers, safeguards His own call, rewards those who believe, and punishes those who disbelieve.

This lesson begins with migration (hijrah). Before it, the Muhajirun and Ansar were granted permission to fight (jihad), because the defence of the Islamic way of life is not possible without jihad. As long as they do not strive, they can neither worship Allah, nor perform their acts of worship, nor protect their own lives or their religion. Do they not see that they have been expelled from their city without any crime? Indeed, their only "crime" was that they acknowledged Allah alone as their Lord. Allah consoles them: since they left their city and abandoned their wealth and property, it is Allah Himself who will reward them for this deed.

In connection with this, a general principle is stated: whoever is wronged may retaliate to the same extent as the wrong done to him. If the oppressor, after this, goes further in oppression and wrongs again, then Allah will be with the oppressed. Allah gives evidence for this promise: Allah is able to help, because it is He who runs this entire universe, and part of the sunnah and the established order (namus) according to which this universe operates is that the oppressed be given help.

After this, the address turns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): every nation has a manhaj (way of life), it has been commanded to follow it, and it has been prepared for it. The Messenger (ﷺ) is told to state this plainly to the polytheists and not to give them an opportunity to dispute with him. If they nevertheless engage in argument (mujadalah), then leave the matter to Allah. He will judge on the Day of Resurrection, for true knowledge lies with Him who knows everything in the heavens and the earth. What proof do these people have regarding the idols they worship? They cling to their position without evidence, because they detest hearing the word of truth, and this aversion dominates them to such an extent that when the verses are recited to them, there is a danger they may attack those who recite them. Allah warns them: do not hasten; the fire is prepared for you, and the time is coming soon.

Then the weakness of those false deities that are invoked besides Allah is described, and this is presented as a general message addressed to all of humanity. The helplessness of these deities is described in a manner that is highly contemptuous: they cannot even overcome a fly. This lesson concludes with the point that the Muslim community must fulfil its duties. What are these duties? That it is the guardian of all humanity. For this, its moral preparation is ruku', sujud and the doing of good deeds; establishing the system of prayer, establishing the system of zakat, and placing trust in Allah. With this, this surah also concludes.

Commentary on the verses

Those who emigrated... (verse 58–59)

The meaning of migration in the way of Allah is that a person gives up all those things which the self desires, which it holds very dear and for which it is greatly covetous: family, city, homeland, memories of the past, wealth and the provisions of life. To sacrifice all these things for one's ideology, to seek the pleasure of Allah, and to look toward the reward that is with Allah, is a matter so valuable that it surpasses this world and all that it contains.

The command of hijrah was before the conquest of Makkah, and it began when the Islamic state was established in Madinah. After the conquest of Makkah, if someone left other lands and came to Madinah, it was not regarded as hijrah, though it was certainly regarded as jihad and a righteous deed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that after the conquest of Makkah, if someone performs jihad, it will be considered a good deed and will bring reward.

"Those who emigrated in the way of Allah and were then killed or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision" (22:58). Whether they were martyred or died a natural death, because they abandoned their country and wealth and set out prepared for that outcome. They preferred martyrdom and sacrificed the most cherished wealth and country of the world. Therefore Allah too decided a great reward for them in every circumstance.

"And indeed Allah is the best of providers" (22:58). The provision that Allah has announced for them is far better than what they left behind.

"He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with" (22:59). They set out toward the place upon which Allah's pleasure rests, so He will admit them into a place with which they will be content. This is a great honour for them, that Allah prepares for them a place of their own choosing, although they are His servants and He is their Creator.

"And indeed Allah is Knowing and Forbearing" (22:59). Allah knows the oppression they suffered, and He knows what they desire. And He is Forbearing in that He gives everyone respite, and then He will give both the oppressor and the oppressed their full recompense.

The situation of human beings is that when they are oppressed, sometimes they are patient and sometimes they are not. When they are not patient, they respond to the oppression, and in the face of such afflictions they inflict similar afflictions on their enemies. If the oppressors still do not desist, Allah takes upon Himself the responsibility that He will assist the oppressed.

ذلک ……غفور (06)

The condition for this support is that the punishment was given as retaliation (qisas), without excess, and that it was not changed into oppression through transgression. The punishment should not have been exaggerated.

After permitting this punishment, the verse says that Allah is Ghafur and Rahim. If a person is wronged and takes balanced retaliation for it, but the oppressor again rises up in oppression, then the promise of Allah's support is with the person who took retaliation, not with the oppressor and the rebel. However, Allah links this promise with the universal laws of nature (nawamis takwini qudrat) of this cosmos. Why? Because these cosmic laws of divine power bear witness that Allah has power over everything and that He is able to give support. Secondly, just as these laws of nature are unchangeable and fulfil their duties with the utmost precision, in the same way Allah's support is also a cosmic reality. It is simply not possible that it should not happen.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verse 61:

ذلک بان اللہ ……بصیر (16)

This is a natural cosmic scene that passes before our eyes every day and night. We observe its effects in the form of summer and winter. At the time of sunset the night enters the day, and at the time of sunrise the day enters the night. In the same way, the night enters the day and in winter diminishes the limits of the day, and the day enters the night and in summer diminishes the limits of the night. A person keeps seeing these scenes, day and night, that the day enters the night and the night enters the day, but because of great familiarity and great repetition these strange and wondrous scenes have ceased to be captivating for us, and we do not reflect on how finely this system is running. Not even for a minute does any disturbance occur in it. This system never stops. This fact is a testimony to the power of the Almighty who has set this system in motion.

The Qur'an draws our attention to this scene: why do you pass by such scenes with such heedlessness, so that it may show you what the state of Allah's power is? From one side He rolls up their expanse, extinguishes the night, and from the other side He removes the darkness and spreads out the light of the day. This system is so fine that no disruption enters it; centuries have passed. The same is the case with the help that has been announced in support of the oppressed. It is as certain as this system of night and day is certain. In this way Allah is now rolling up the system of the kingdoms of tyrants and establishing in the world the system of life of the righteous and just people. This political revolution too is as certain and unalterable as the revolution of day and night, and it is a cosmic sunnah. This sunnah too flows on like night and day, but people are heedless of it, just as they are heedless of the signs of the cosmos in this universe, although these signs are before their eyes every moment in the form of an open book.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verse 62:

ذلک بان اللہ ……العلی الکبیر (36)

This proves that Allah is the Truth (al-Haqq), and that the Truth controls this system of the universe. Whatever exists besides Allah is falsehood (batil). Falsehood keeps suffering disruption, while the Truth remains established and enduring. Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)

Rain falling from the sky, the earth becoming green and fresh, and this scene repeating morning and evening: this is a process that is repeated before our eyes again and again, and we have become so familiar with it that it is as if nothing had happened. But if we awaken our consciousness like a poet, this scene stirs countless feelings within hearts and minds. A person feels that this small plant which splits the earth and emerges its head, coming out of soil and mud, is like a little child who comes out into this world and laughs, and there is a refreshing smile on its face. It seems that this small plant might fly away in its joy.

Only those who possess such consciousness can understand this verse.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Aware﴾ (22:63). "Subtle" means that He sees even the finest detail and is aware of it. He observes this scene with great gentleness and depth, and He is the Creator and Knower of the reality and nature of these scenes.

It is the gentleness and kindness of Allah that this small plant emerges from the earth, although it is extremely weak and powerless; the hand of divine power lifts it up into the air, and despite the earth's attraction and the pull of gravity, it has within it the desire to rise and grow. It is the gentleness and kindness of divine power that rain falls at the exact time, in the right amount, and that this water mixes with the soil in a most precise manner, plant processes begin, and then living plant cells start their journey towards the light.

Allah is the Owner of the heavens, the earth and what is between them. He is free of need from the heavens, the earth and what is between them. He gives living things the provision of water and plants, yet He Himself is free of need from both provision and those who receive provision.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth … the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ (46)

He has no need of any creature in the heavens or on the earth. He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani), the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid), the Laudable (al-Mahmud), and His generosity extends over all creation.

The discussion on this theme moves further, pointing out that in this very universe, which lies before their eyes and is vast, there are things for people to reflect upon.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 22, verse 65:

الم تر ……رحیم (56)

[Verse 22:65 ff. — "Have you not seen..." through "...Merciful (56)"]

What power there is in this earth, what wealth! And Allah has made these powers and stores subservient to human beings, yet man is heedless of these blessings of Allah. He is immersed in these blessings night and day, yet he lies heedless.

Allah has made everything in the heavens and the earth beneficial and subservient to man. He has made the natural laws of this universe conform to and suit human nature. If Allah had made the physical conditions of this earth opposed to the physical conditions of man, then living here would have been difficult for man, let alone his being able to benefit from the store of this universe. If man's physical make-up were different, and on this globe he could not walk, could not draw breath, could not take nourishment, could not drink water, then man could not remain alive here even for a moment. If man's weight were not as suitably balanced as it is, then his feet would not stay firm on the earth; he would either fly into the air or sink into the ground. If there were no air on the earth, or if it were even slightly denser than its present state, his throat would be choked and he would die immediately. Therefore, it is indeed the command of Allah, and the work of that Subtle, All-Aware One, that He made these natural powers suitable for man and made man suitable for them.

On the one hand, Allah gave man such power that he could subdue this globe; on the other hand, He made the earth and the powers hidden within it such that they kept coming under human control. Whenever man has needed some new power, He has caused him to discover that new power. When it occurred to him that some store of the earth's resources was about to run out, he found a new store. Before petrol reserves had run out, he discovered atomic energy, and before he had gained full control over it, he discovered hydrogen power. Now the third stage: how there will be life after death. This too is one of the hidden knowledge of Allah, an unseen matter. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verse 70:

﴿Do you not know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ (22: 08)

Is there anything in the heavens and the earth that is not within Allah's knowledge? Everything is recorded in a Book. For Allah, this is not difficult at all. Allah's knowledge is extremely complete and extremely precise, and nothing in this universe is hidden from Him. He is not affected by anything that causes something to be erased or forgotten. All of this is inscribed in a Book, and keeping such a record is not difficult for Allah.

The human intellect grows weary. Especially when it reflects on this comprehensive system, the intellect becomes exhausted. When we consider the all-encompassing nature of Allah's knowledge regarding this entire universe, and try to grasp it in our minds, and feel that countless things, persons, actions, intentions, thoughts and movements exist in the visible world and in the hidden world, then the fabric of our imagination is torn apart. Yet, in relation to Allah's knowledge and power, this is an easy matter.

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ (22: 08) After giving the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the guidance that he should not give the polytheists any opportunity for disputation, so that they would not argue against his straight path, now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is made to understand that their own way and their own manhaj (method) leave room for argument. In it there is crookedness, weakness, ignorance, injustice and all other deficiencies. Because these people are followers of falsehood, they are also deprived of Allah's support and assistance. They have no helper.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verse 71:

{Wa ya'budūna ... min naṣīr} (17)

The reality is that in this world, any situation, law or society that does not have sanction from Allah has no real power. Whatever lacks the power of Allah behind it is weak. The fundamental element of strength, which is the authority of Allah (sultan Ilahi), is simply not present in it.

These people are idol-worshippers, human-worshippers or devil-worshippers. Over all these things there is no divine hand, and therefore such people are deprived of true strength. They worship the above-mentioned things without any proof, any knowledge or any basis of certainty. They accept them only on the foundation of illusion and superstition. When they have been deprived of the help and support of Allah, then in this world and the Hereafter they have no helper or supporter.

The astonishing thing is that these people worship, besides Allah, things for which Allah has sent down no sanction or justification, and they have no knowledge of them. Yet they are neither ready to listen to the call of truth nor do they accept it. Rather, these people, out of obstinacy, have become ready to engage in sinful acts, and they have fallen into such stubbornness and enmity that it appears as though they would pounce upon the bearer of the divine message before them and tear him apart and devour him.

And when Our verses are recited to them ... ﴿and when Our verses are recited to them﴾

These people do not answer an argument with an argument, nor do they refute an argument with an argument. Instead, in the face of an argument they become angry and want to devour their opponent. This is a sign that they have no argument, and the last resort of rebellious people is that they break out in fighting and resort to violence. They do not want to hear a word of truth. They speak with the argument of the stick, because they know that they have nothing but the stick. For this reason the Quran gives them this answer:

﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? It is the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve. And wretched is the destination."﴾ (22:72)

Say to them: "Shall I tell you of something worse than that? Fire, which Allah has promised to those who refuse to accept the truth, and what a wretched destination it is."

That is, if you answer argument with the stick, then there is a greater power against your power. Face it, and wait for the outcome. But remember that the outcome is a very wretched one.

...

Now comes the general announcement of this surah, a resolution for all people, stated forcefully and in a loud voice: O people, reflect a little on your deities. Whoever worships any kind of deity other than Allah seeks help from it, in whatever form it may be, and it is something that is called upon. Allah shows their weakness and feebleness through a clear example that can be seen and heard. What is the example? It is a depiction of a moving, living scene. Upon seeing this scene, the eyes brighten and the heart rejoices. Now look closely at this scene and witness the helplessness of those gods.

"O people" — this is a general call, an announcement made in a loud voice to all.

Yā ayyuhā al-nās (22:73, cited here as 22:38 in the Urdu text's numbering). O people, when the people have gathered, a parable is set before them, in the form of a remarkable scene. This is not a specific assembly, nor an incidental matter; rather, people have been summoned.

Ḍarb mathal, fa-stami'ū lahu (22:73): "A parable is presented; listen carefully to it." This parable establishes a rule and principle and conveys a reality.

"Indeed, those whom you call upon besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose" (22:73).

That is, the idols you worship besides Allah, or the persons whom you serve as lords, or the customs and traditions you serve as lords, from whom you seek help, from whom you seek assistance, and from whom you seek honour: all of them, even if they were to combine, could not create a single fly. The fly is among the smallest and most insignificant of Allah's creatures, yet those whom these people call deities and gods are not capable even of this. Though they all came together to aid one another, they could not create this most trivial of Allah's creations.

As far as the creation of a fly is concerned, it is as difficult and impossible as the creation of large animals such as the camel and the elephant, because the fly contains the same secret of life as the camel and the elephant. Thus, in terms of being impossible for creatures, small and great are equal. But the miraculous mode of expression of the Qur'an has chosen here a thing as small and insignificant as the fly as the example, because if someone is unable to create a fly, his inability is more easily understood in comparison to a camel or an elephant. This is merely a figurative mode of expression; otherwise, in reality, both are the same. This is a most unique style of the noble Qur'an.

Now, step a little further in the direction of the weakness of these deities.

"And if the fly should snatch anything away from them, they could not rescue it from it" (22:73). That is, the condition of these deities is such that if a fly snatches something from them, they cannot recover it, whether they be idols, or persons and saints. Indeed, even great Pharaohs cannot seize back something that a fly has carried off from them. Here too the fly is chosen so that the shadow of this small and insignificant thing falls upon these idols and their helplessness is clearly manifested. Moreover, the fly carries dangerous diseases, and it snatches away refined things from us. Sometimes it takes away our eyesight, sometimes a limb becomes paralysed because of it, and sometimes a person even loses his life to this affliction. It carries the germs of tuberculosis, typhoid, dysentery and cholera, yet it takes from us things that we cannot take back from it.

The miraculous style of the Qur'an, by selecting one such word and concept, creates this atmosphere. If the Qur'an had said that if beasts of prey snatched anything from them they could not rescue it, this would have conveyed the notion of strength in contrast to weakness; yet beasts of prey cannot snatch anything more valuable than a fly. But by the word "fly," the sense of their helplessness and contemptibility becomes far more profound.

The parable concludes with these words:

"Weak are the seeker and the sought" (22:73). That is, those who seek help are weak, and those from whom help is sought are also weak, so that the atmosphere of weakness created by the word "fly" is confirmed. Now the atmosphere is prepared: the contemptibility and helplessness of these deities has settled into human thought and reflection. In such an atmosphere the Qur'an proclaims the power of Allah, and at the same time it is regrettable that humanity has not appraised this great power of Allah.

﴿Ma qadarul-Allāha ḥaqqa qadrihi, inna Allāha la-qawiyyun ʿazīz﴾ (47)
