Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 22, verses 77–78:

یایھا الذین ……النصیر (47)

In these two verses, a complete methodology (manhaj) is placed before the Muslim community. The duties and requirements that are attached as essential conditions to this methodology and system are also laid out. What is its importance? And how far do its roots extend in the past and the present, when this methodology and system were established in accordance with Allah's desire? What is this methodology?

٭ The believers are first commanded to bow (ruku') and prostrate (sujud). Ruku' and sujud are distinguished fundamental pillars of Islam. The Holy Qur'an often expresses prayer (salah) by means of ruku' and sujud, because these are the important parts of prayer and, when presenting the scene of prayer, they are the outward actions that relate to vivid depiction. This is because the Qur'an's style of expression is in the form of scenes, which is an engaging manner, and it has a greater effect on consciousness.

٭ After the most distinguished worship and its most distinguished pillars, there is a general command that encompasses the entire life: servitude ('ubudiyyah), which is more comprehensive than prayer. This is because worship includes obligations and also includes every act about which Allah has a command and which is performed seeking Allah's pleasure. Likewise, all movements of human life can be turned into worship if they are performed with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure. Even those matters of life that relate to enjoyment can become worship if Allah is mentioned over them, thanks is rendered to Allah, and the intention is made that by using these blessings we will further worship and perform jihad. Anything can become worship through intention alone, and pure worship can become mere play through intention alone.

٭ That Islam is nothing but good; all good deeds constitute the Islamic system of life. Prayer, servitude and goodness are the essence of the Islamic system.

Now this Islam must be implemented in the practical world, and you can succeed in this by doing good deeds. Your connection with Allah through the servitude and worship of Allah will become strong, and by doing good deeds your practical life will be set right. Through this, the direction of your collective life will be set on the path of faith. When the community has been trained such that its connection with Allah has been firmly established through worship, and its practical life has been founded on obedience to Allah and doing good, then the community, or some group within the community, will be ready to bear the responsibility which is the sole method for establishing the Islamic system. And what is that?

وجاھدوا فی اللہ حق جھادہ (22 : 88) "Strive in the cause of Allah with the striving that is due to Him." This is an extremely comprehensive expression: fulfil the right of jihad. Through this it is conveyed that this responsibility is very great. It requires very great preparation and has very great demands. Strive in the path of Allah as the right of striving requires: strive against the enemies of Allah, strive against your own self, strive against mischief and every evil. Fulfil the right of striving in the path of Allah; indeed you have been prepared for jihad for this great duty. From among all of humanity, you have been chosen.

ھو اجتبکم (22 : 88) "He has chosen you." Then, since Allah has chosen you, your responsibility has increased compared to others. Now there is no path left for resignation or flight. This is a bounty from Allah to this community and group, and it is fitting that we give thanks to Allah and carry out this task well.

Then Allah's mercy is also included with it. The task is also easy.

وما جعل علیکم فی الدین من حرج (22 : 88) "He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion." This religion, its obligations, its worships, its laws and its ethics have taken into consideration human nature, and the natural powers of human beings have been directed towards constructive works. They have not been restrained the way gas is restrained, nor have these powers been left free like animals. Moreover, this religion is a methodology whose roots extend deep into the history of the past.

ملۃ ابیکم ابرھیم (22 : 88) "Adhere to the creed of your father Ibrahim."

This religion is indeed the fountainhead of monotheism (tawhid), and its origin connects to Hazrat Ibrahim. Therefore it is not the case that its roots are not on the earth, nor is there any major gap (GAP) in its history, as there was between the messengerships before Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Its name too is historical: Hazrat Ibrahim has named you "Muslims", and has named this creed the Islamic community (millat-e-islamiyyah).

The very meaning of Islam is that you turn your faces, intentions and deeds all towards God. Therefore, from the first day, the Muslim community has had one ideology, one belief and one qiblah. From Hazrat Ibrahim up to Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) there is one chain, one system and one message. Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) was entrusted with this trust last of all, and was commanded that this message must be conveyed to all of humanity.

لیکون الرسول شھیدا علیکم و تکونوا شھدآء علی الناس (22 : 88) "That the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over the people." So the Messenger is a witness over the community, meaning that he will establish a system for it, teach the distinction between right and wrong and good and evil; and this same duty this community will discharge with respect to other people. This community is, as it were, the overseer of all of humanity. The legal values of this community require that its training and its thinking also be along this line. This community would not be the Muslim community if it did not oversee all of humanity and did not discharge its essential duty.

As long as the Muslim community kept the Islamic system of life implemented in its own homes and lives, it remained the overseer of the whole world. When this community deviated from the system of the Shariah and abandoned the performance of its obligations, Allah the Exalted removed it from the position of leadership and made it a mere follower of others, and now it will remain thus always, until it again possesses the Islamic system.

It cannot discharge this duty until it prepares for it, and the prescription for preparation has been told by Allah: that you establish prayer, that you give zakat, and that you place complete trust in Allah.

فاقیموا الصلوۃ ……النصیر (22 : 88) "So establish prayer, give zakat, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper."

٭ Prayer establishes the connection of a frail and mortal human being with that Being who is strong and the possessor of all power.

٭ Zakat is the establishment of kinship (silat al-rahm) among the members of the Muslim community and the Muslim group. It is the arrangement for supporting the members of the group in their needs and necessities, so that corruption does not arise.

٭ And trust in Allah is the firm rope which one should never let go of.

These are the implements of war through which this community can discharge the duty of bearing witness over humanity, for which it was raised up. And apart from these moral weapons, there is a general guidance for the community that it may also gather conventional ground weapons to the extent of steadfastness. The Qur'an has not been heedless of this. But here Allah emphasizes that power, that military training and that equipment, which is the sole weapon of the Muslim community and which no one else possesses: namely, connection with Allah, righteousness and reform, and a lofty outlook and exalted dignity.

The fundamental aim before the Islamic system is that humanity be brought to that perfection which is attainable on this earth. Islam here does not merely emphasize animal-like material progress as animals do, but also emphasizes spiritual progress.

The lofty values of humanity also take into consideration the material needs of man, but they do not confine their activities merely to material needs, and this is precisely the demand of Islam from the Muslim community: that the leadership of the world be conducted in the light of Islam's comprehensive system.

Ṣadaqa Allāh al-ʿAẓīm.

یایھا الذین ……النصیر (47)

In these two verses, a complete methodology (manhaj) is placed before the Muslim community. The duties and requirements that are attached as essential conditions to this methodology and system are also laid out. What is its importance? And how far do its roots extend in the past and the present, when this methodology and system were established in accordance with Allah's desire? What is this methodology?

٭ The believers are first commanded to bow (ruku') and prostrate (sujud). Ruku' and sujud are distinguished fundamental pillars of Islam. The Holy Qur'an often expresses prayer (salah) by means of ruku' and sujud, because these are the important parts of prayer and, when presenting the scene of prayer, they are the outward actions that relate to vivid depiction. This is because the Qur'an's style of expression is in the form of scenes, which is an engaging manner, and it has a greater effect on consciousness.

٭ After the most distinguished worship and its most distinguished pillars, there is a general command that encompasses the entire life: servitude ('ubudiyyah), which is more comprehensive than prayer. This is because worship includes obligations and also includes every act about which Allah has a command and which is performed seeking Allah's pleasure. Likewise, all movements of human life can be turned into worship if they are performed with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure. Even those matters of life that relate to enjoyment can become worship if Allah is mentioned over them, thanks is rendered to Allah, and the intention is made that by using these blessings we will further worship and perform jihad. Anything can become worship through intention alone, and pure worship can become mere play through intention alone.

٭ That Islam is nothing but good; all good deeds constitute the Islamic system of life. Prayer, servitude and goodness are the essence of the Islamic system.

Now this Islam must be implemented in the practical world, and you can succeed in this by doing good deeds. Your connection with Allah through the servitude and worship of Allah will become strong, and by doing good deeds your practical life will be set right. Through this, the direction of your collective life will be set on the path of faith.
